avoid_supplements.name: St. John's Wort
avoid_supplements.mechanism: Induces CYP3A4 and glucuronidation; increases carbamazepine metabolism and reduces serum levels, risking seizure breakthrough
avoid_supplements.action: Contraindicated; do not use concurrently. Counsel patient to avoid all herbal products containing St. John's Wort

avoid_supplements.name: Ginkgo biloba
avoid_supplements.mechanism: May induce CYP3A4 metabolism; potential reduction in carbamazepine efficacy
avoid_supplements.action: Avoid concurrent use; recommend alternative cognitive support strategies if needed

avoid_supplements.name: Ginseng (American and Asian)
avoid_supplements.mechanism: CYP3A4 enzyme induction; may decrease carbamazepine plasma concentrations
avoid_supplements.action: Discontinue use; monitor seizure control if patient has been using concurrently

caution_supplements.name: Folate/Folic Acid
caution_supplements.mechanism: Carbamazepine increases folate metabolism; supplementation may be beneficial but does not alter drug metabolism
caution_supplements.action: Monitor folate levels; supplementation may be recommended, especially in women of childbearing age due to teratogenic risk

caution_supplements.name: Vitamin D
caution_supplements.mechanism: Carbamazepine induces CYP24A1 and increases vitamin D metabolism; deficiency risk with long-term use
caution_supplements.action: Monitor vitamin D levels periodically; supplementation often recommended to maintain bone health

caution_supplements.name: Calcium
caution_supplements.mechanism: Carbamazepine impairs calcium absorption and bone metabolism; supplementation may offset deficiency risk
caution_supplements.action: Consider supplementation; monitor bone health parameters in long-term users

avoid_foods.name: Grapefruit and Grapefruit Juice
avoid_foods.mechanism: CYP3A4 inhibition increases carbamazepine bioavailability and serum levels, raising toxicity risk
avoid_foods.action: Eliminate grapefruit products from diet; counsel patient on all citrus products to avoid

caution_foods.name: High-fiber foods (excessive amounts)
caution_foods.mechanism: May reduce gastrointestinal absorption of carbamazepine if intake is excessive
caution_foods.action: Maintain consistent, moderate fiber intake; separate high-fiber meals from drug administration by 2 hours if possible

caution_foods.name: Alcohol
caution_foods.mechanism: CNS depression additive effect; alcohol may also induce carbamazepine metabolism with chronic use
caution_foods.action: Limit or avoid alcohol; counsel patient on increased sedation and dizziness risk

monitoring_notes: Carbamazepine is a potent CYP3A4 inducer requiring vigilant monitoring for interactions with many medications and supplements. Regular serum level monitoring (therapeutic range: 4-12 mcg/mL) is essential, particularly when supplements or dietary changes are introduced, as carbamazepine levels may fluctuate significantly.
